claim_formal: ∀ abelian variety A/Q̄ with good reduction A_0 at w, ∀ rational Hodge class γ ∈ H^{2r}, ∀ divisors D_1..D_{d-r} on A_0: the pairings Tr(γ_0·c_1(D_1)⋯c_1(D_{d-r})) in all ℓ-adic (ℓ≠p) and crystalline realizations equal one common rational number q

quote_A.text: After good reduction, the pairing of a rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-p realization and in crystalline cohomology.

quote_B.text: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including residue characteristic 2.

notes: Theorem literally reads 'there is a number q∈Q such that ...' so a literal reading gives prefix ∀∃ with M2; labelled ∀/M1 because the content is a rationality/independence property. Corollary: every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle (uses Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties, cf. family 032).

claim_formal: ∀ E/Q, ∀ prime q: s_q(E)∈{0,1} → r(E)=ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_q(E) ∧ #Ш(E/Q)<∞ ∧ L^{(r)}(E,1)/r! = Ω_E Reg_E #Ш ∏c_ℓ / #E(Q)_tors²

quote_A.text: If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E),\qquad \#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty, \]

quote_B.text: We prove the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one at some prime q.

notes: BSD settled in the Selmer-corank ≤1 range. The rank/finiteness part comes from the companion all-prime Selmer converse and the 2-primary part from the companion 2-primary BSD paper (both OpenAI manuscripts in this family); the new step is the odd-prime valuation. M7 (identity) is an alternative for the leading-term formula. Secondary results: unrestricted Selmer converse, Sylvester cube sums for ℓ≡4,7,8 mod 9.

claim_formal: ∀ q ≥1, ∀ Dirichlet character χ mod q, ∀ s ∈ ℂ with Re s > 7/8 and ¬(χ principal ∧ s=1): L(s,χ) ≠ 0 (in particular ζ(s)≠0 for Re s>7/8)

quote_A.text: all Dirichlet L-functions are zero-free in the half-plane $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$

quote_B.text: In particular, the Riemann zeta function is zero-free in this half-plane, proving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

notes: Zero-free half-plane read as non-existence of zeros (M4); M1 or M8 (sup Re ρ ≤ 7/8) are plausible alternatives. Lean DirichletSevenEighths matches the Dirichlet headline (QuasiRiemannHypothesis comparator covers only ζ, a weaker special case); the Hecke L-functions over Q(√-3) part is not in the comparator. Companions: alternate 11/12 proof; uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros (own Lean). Corollaries: Vinogradov least nonresidue, deterministic square roots, Euler's idoneal numbers.

claim_formal: ¬∃ algorithm A such that ∀ n, ∀ f ∈ Z[X_1..X_n]: A(f) decides whether ∃ x ∈ Q^n with f(x)=0

quote_A.text: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial $f\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\Q^n$.

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers

notes: Second manuscript in the input (pointwise 2-converse for curves with rational 2-torsion) is unrelated to the headline. H10 over Q is not literally on Hilbert's list (that is over Z), so P2 rather than P3.

claim_formal: G = Σ_{j≥0} (-1)^j/(2j+1)² is irrational

quote_A.text: Catalan's constant is irrational.

quote_B.text: We prove that Catalan's constant $`G=\sum_{j\geq0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2`$ is irrational.

notes: Long-standing expected irrationality treated as a named conjecture (P1); P2 possible if not considered a conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀ E/Q, ∀ j∈{0,1}: lim_{X→∞} #{d squarefree, 0<|d|≤X : ord_{s=1}L(E^{(d)},s)=j} / #{d squarefree, 0<|d|≤X} = 1/2

quote_A.text: \lim_{X\to\infty} \frac{\#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):a(E^{(d)})=j\}}{\#\mathcal D(X)} =\frac12.

quote_B.text: We prove Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture: for every elliptic curve E over ℚ, the quadratic twists of E with analytic rank zero and one each have density 1/2

notes: Density theorem follows from the new pointwise 2-converse plus Smith's Selmer-corank distribution (prior result). Mean analytic rank 1/2 proved in companion manuscript via tail estimate. Counting convention is signed squarefree d by |d|, not Goldfeld's fundamental discriminants.

quote_A.text: \left|\sum_{1\le n\le X} \lambda(a_1n+b_1)\lambda(a_2n+b_2)\right| \le C_{a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2}\frac{X}{(\log X)^c} \qquad(X\ge3).

quote_B.text: We prove the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture.

notes: Literal prefix is ∃c∀(forms)∃C∀X; constants treated as part of the bound so prefix ∀ (∃∀ also defensible). Two-point case of Chowla's k-point conjecture; labelled O1 because the binary ordinary case is posed as its own conjecture, O5 is the alternative. Also proves binary corrected Elliott conjecture for uniformly nonpretentious functions (own Lean theorem). Implied constants need not be effective.

claim_formal: ∃ homogeneous σ_{2k+1} ∈ W_{2k+1} (k≥1) such that Lie_Q⟨e_3,e_5,…⟩ → (grt=W,{,}), e_{2k+1}↦σ_{2k+1}, is an isomorphism of graded Lie algebras (and on weight completions)

quote_A.text: the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is freely generated by one element in every odd weight at least three

quote_B.text: We prove the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture

notes: Statement about the specific object grt; theorem and Lean phrase it as ∃ generators / ∃ linear iso, so prefix ∃ is the alternative.

claim_formal: ∀ prime ℓ, ∀ f.g. K/k, L/l over algebraically closed k,l with char ≠ ℓ and trdeg ≥ 2: the canonical map Isom^i_F(K,L) → Isom_M(K^M_1(K)/ℓ, K^M_1(L)/ℓ)/F_ℓ^× (compatible with K^M_2/ℓ product) is bijective

quote_A.text: Then \eqref{eq:main-map} is bijective. In particular, a compatible isomorphism $V_K\to V_L$ forces equality of the characteristics and of the relative transcendence degrees.

quote_B.text: We prove a mod-ℓ Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction theorem for function fields of transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from ℓ.

notes: Bijectivity of a canonical Isom map read as M7 (M1/M5 alternatives). Summary headline is the mod-ℓ Milnor K-theory reconstruction, not itself called a conjecture (P2, low confidence); family also proves the equal-characteristic version and the Bogomolov–Pop conjecture (P1/O1) for pro-ℓ abelian-by-central Galois data. Lean comparator is only injectivity for the Galois (Bogomolov–Pop) version, hence 'different'.

claim_formal: ∀ finite E/Q_2, ∀ continuous odd absolutely irreducible r: G_Q → GL_2(E) unramified outside finitely many primes: ∃ odd N, ∃ continuous λ: T_2(N) → O_E with λ(T_ℓ)=tr r(Frob_ℓ), λ(ℓS_ℓ)=det r(Frob_ℓ) for ℓ∤2N

quote_A.text: Then there exist an odd positive integer $N$, divisible by every odd prime where $r$ ramifies, and a continuous $\Z_2$-algebra homomorphism \[ \lambda:\mathbb T_2(N)\longrightarrow\OO_E \]

quote_B.text: Emerton records this expectation for the full varying-weight algebra in \cite[Conjecture~2.12]{Emerton2011Families}. That formulation prescribes the allowed tame primes. Theorem~\ref{thm:main} proves dyadic occurrence

notes: Pro-modularity settled at p=2 only (Emerton's conjecture is for all p) and with auxiliary tame primes allowed, so O5; O1 if the p=2 case is regarded as its own problem. Companions: Emerton's dimension conjecture at p=2 (Krull dim 4) and the odd regular 2-dim Fontaine–Mazur conjecture at 2 (classical modularity up to twist).

claim_formal: For p uniform among primes ≤ x: ∀ k, ∀ bounded continuous F on [0,1]^k: E[F(V_1(p),…,V_k(p))] → E[F(L_1,…,L_k)] as x→∞, where V_j=log q_j(p)/log(p-1) and (L_j) ~ PD(1)

quote_A.text: As $`x\to\infty`$, their logarithms, divided by $`\log(p-1)`$, converge in every finite joint distribution to the Poisson–Dirichlet distribution with parameter one.

quote_B.text: This proves the conjecture of Ford, Konyagin and Luca.

notes: Prefix ℙ by tie-break 4 (limit law of a uniformly random prime); the theorem itself is a ∀k ∀F averaged limit, so ∀ is the alternative. Also resolves Granville's shifted-prime Dickman asymptotic. Family also proves Erdős's totient-fiber conjecture (g(n)>n^{1-ε} infinitely often), smooth shifted primes x^{1-o(1)}, and infinitely many primes with μ(p-1)=1.

quote_A.text: \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X \#\{2\leq n\leq X:\Pplus(n)\leq n^a, \ \Pplus(n+1)\leq n^b\} =\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b).

quote_B.text: This resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture positively and implies that the ordering $`P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)`$ has natural density 1/2.

notes: Corollary: density of P+(n)<P+(n+1) is 1/2 (Erdős–Turán comparison question). Lean namespace mentions Erdos970 but that appears to be a shared library name, so not counted as an Erdős-database entry (P3 would apply if it is one).

claim_formal: ∀ A,B ⊆ Z_{≥0} with |A|,|B| ≥ 2: (A+B) △ P is infinite

quote_A.text: no set differing from the primes by finitely many elements can be written as $`A+B`$, where A and B are sets of nonnegative integers with at least two elements each.

quote_B.text: We prove Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture

claim_formal: ∀ k=F̄_q (or alg. closed char p with p very good, p∤|W_G|), ∀ smooth projective connected curve X/k, ∀ connected reductive G satisfying the four characteristic hypotheses: L_G^restr: Shv_Nilp(Bun_G(X)) ≃ IndCoh_Nilp(LocSys^restr) is an equivalence

quote_A.text: Consequently the given functor is a $\QCoh(Y)$-linear equivalence \[ \mathbb L_G^{\mathrm{restr}}: \Shv_{\Nilp}(\Bun_G(X))\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \IndCoh_{\Nilp}(Y). \]

quote_B.text: This proves Gaitsgory–Raskin's full-support conjecture [[12, Conjecture 1.3.10]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02237v1) in these regimes.

notes: Conjecture proved only under characteristic hypotheses ('in these regimes'), hence O5. Bundle of 8 manuscripts: generic Ramanujan for exceptional groups at all places and unramified Ramanujan for generic cuspidal reps (O1-type results), Ramanujan–Arthur decompositions proving GLR Conjectures 3.4.5–3.4.6 at trivial level, rationality of the Arthur filtration, conditional global Arthur enhancements (conditional_on the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition), tame Hecke eigensheaf constructions.

claim_formal: ∀ prime n≥5, ∀ sequences (K_i,M_i,σ_i) of totally real degree-n fields with full lattices and D(M_i)→∞: μ_{K_i,M_i,σ_i} → m_n weakly (Haar measure on SL_n(Z)\SL_n(R)), no escape of mass

quote_A.text: For every fixed prime $n\ge5$ and every sequence $(K_i,M_i,\sigma_i)$ as above with \mbox{$D(M_i)\to\infty$}, \[ \mu_{K_i,M_i,\sigma_i}\longrightarrow m_n. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the packet form of the higher-dimensional Duke equidistribution problem for totally real fields of any fixed prime degree at least five

notes: Equidistribution to Haar read as a determined limit (M9); M1 (convergence property) is the alternative. Problem settled in prime degrees ≥5, primitive quartic and primitive sextic fields only; composite degrees in general remain, hence O5. P1 vs P2 uncertain (framed as 'Duke equidistribution problem'). Lean comparator matches the prime-degree theorem.

claim_formal: ∀ number field K, ∀ abelian variety A/K, ∀ irreducible X ⊆ A_{K̄}: the set of maximal atypical subvarieties of X relative to S=⟨X⟩_sp is finite

quote_A.text: there are only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties of $X$ in $S=\langle X\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}$.

quote_B.text: We prove the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over $`\overline{\mathbb Q}`$.

notes: Finiteness statement labelled M1 (M8/M4 conceivable). Proved over Q̄, which is the standard arithmetic setting; O5 if the conjecture over C is taken as the posed version. Family also proves the full curve case of Zilber–Pink in A_2 for Hodge-generic curves over Q̄ (E×CM, QM and E² branches).

claim_formal: μ(π) = 2, i.e. ∀ ν>2 ∃ Q(ν) ∀ p,q ∈ Z with q ≥ Q(ν): |π − p/q| ≥ q^{−ν}

quote_A.text: The irrationality exponent of \(\pi\) is \(2\).

quote_B.text: We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of π is 2.

notes: Tie-break 7: posed number determined exactly → M9/O1 (previous record 7.103...). Threshold Q(ν) not effective. Corollary: Flint–Hills series converges.

claim_formal: ∀ global field k, ∀ absolutely almost simple simply connected G/k, ∀ N ◁ G(k) with N ⊄ Z(G(k)): ∃ open normal W ◁ H_A=∏_{v∈A(G)} G(k_v) with N = δ_A^{-1}(W)

quote_A.text: every noncentral abstract normal subgroup of its rational points is the inverse image of an open normal subgroup of the product of its anisotropic nonarchimedean local groups.

quote_B.text: We prove the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields.

notes: Description of all noncentral normal subgroups read as classification (M6); M2 (∃W) or M5 alternatives. Two manuscripts (number fields; function fields incl. char 2) together give every global field. Corollary: positive-density congruence subgroup property.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p, ∀ finite k/Q_p, ∀ smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/k of genus ≥2: X(k) → {sections of π_1(X) → G_k}/π_1(X_k̄)-conjugacy is bijective

quote_A.text: the map \[ X(k)\longrightarrow \left\{\begin{gathered} s:G_k\to\pi_1(X)\text{ a continuous group homomorphism}

quote_B.text: We prove the local p-adic section conjecture for smooth proper geometrically connected curves of genus at least two, over every finite extension of ℚp.

notes: Bijection between points and section classes read as M7 (M5 alternative). Corollary: global section conjecture over Q for X_0(N), X_1(N) of genus ≥2 (and curves whose finite-descent locus equals rational points). Companion manuscript constructs étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet (geometric input).

claim_formal: ∀ irreducible f ∈ Z[x] of degree 4 with no fixed prime-square divisor: #{1≤n≤X : f(n) squarefree} = c_f X + o(X), c_f = ∏_p (1 − ρ_f(p²)/p²) > 0

quote_A.text: \[ S_{f,k}(X)=c_{f,k}X+o_f(X),\qquad c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0. \]

quote_B.text: We prove that every irreducible integer quartic with no fixed prime-square divisor takes squarefree values with the predicted positive Euler-product density.

notes: Squarefree-values conjecture settled in degree 4 only (general degree ≥5 squarefree remains open), hence O5. Generalization: (d−2)-power-free density for 4≤d≤8, and with Browning for all d≥4. Lean comparator is that all-degree (d−2)-power-free statement, which contains the quartic headline as d=4 (labelled 'same'; strictly it is stronger).

claim_formal: ∃ C>0 ∀ k≥1: h(k) ≤ C k²/(log log 3k)², where h(k) = max over n with ω(n)≤k of the Jacobsthal function j(n)

quote_A.text: There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that \[ h(k)\le C\frac{k^2}{(\log\log(3k))^2} \qquad\text{for every integer }k\ge1. \]

quote_B.text: giving an affirmative answer to Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question.

notes: P3 because the Lean comparator is named erdos_970 (Erdős problem database entry; Erdős recorded the question); otherwise P2. Constant not made explicit. Result goes beyond the asked k² by a (log log k)² saving; separate Lean comparator for the iterated-log version.

claim_formal: ∀ γ ∈ R, ∀ ψ: N → [0,∞): Σ_q φ(q)ψ(q)/q = ∞ → for a.e. x ∈ R, ‖qx − γ‖ < ψ(q) for infinitely many q

quote_A.text: then, for Lebesgue-almost every $x\in\mathbb R$, the inequality \[ \|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q) \] holds for infinitely many positive integers $q$.

quote_B.text: We prove the weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture.

notes: Prefix over γ (∀), ψ (∀, hypothesis-side divergence), x (almost every), q (infinitely many); shorter reading ∀∀ᵍ. Corollary: Hausdorff-measure version via mass transference.

quote_A.text: \sum_{\substack{N\pi\le X\\\pi\equiv1\pmod3\ \mathrm{prime}}}G(\pi) =\frac65c_*\frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X} +o\!\left(\frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X}\right).

quote_B.text: We prove Patterson's first-moment conjecture for normalized cubic Gauss sums over all primary Eisenstein primes, unconditionally.

notes: Single asymptotic formula, no free parameters → none (∀^∞ via the o-term is the alternative). Previously known under GRH (Dunn–Radziwiłł). Also angular-mode cancellation and part of Patterson's complementary conjecture (3∤k).

claim_formal: V(x) ~ (x/log x) G_m A(1;θ) with 0 < inf A ≤ sup A < ∞, and ∀ c>0: V(cx)/V(x) → c

quote_A.text: We give an explicit asymptotic equivalent for $`V(x)`$. Its coefficient is a uniform limit of functions defined from finite arithmetic data.

quote_B.text: We also prove that $`V(cx)/V(x)\to c`$ as $`x\to\infty`$ for every fixed c > 0, answering a question of Erdős and Hall.

notes: Headline is an asymptotic formula for the specific counting function V(x) (open since Ford's bounded-uncertainty estimate); the Erdős–Hall scaling question (P2, answered affirmatively) is the corollary. P3 if the Erdős–Hall question is in the Erdős database.

claim_formal: ∃ c_1,c_2>0 ∀^∞ b: c_1 log log b ≤ N(b) ≤ c_2 log log b, N(b) = max_{1≤a<b} (least number of distinct unit fractions summing to a/b)

quote_A.text: There are absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and $b_0$ such that, for every integer $b\ge b_0$, \[ c_1\log\log b\le N(b)\le c_2\log\log b. \]

quote_B.text: The question appears again in Erd\H{o}s and Graham \cite[pp.~37--38]{ErdosGraham1980} and is recorded as Erd\H{o}s Problem~304 \cite{Bloom304}. Vose subsequently obtained $N(b)\ll\sqrt{\log b}$

notes: New content is the upper bound O(log log b) (M8); with Erdős's classical matching lower bound the order is determined, hence M9. Threshold b_0 unspecified → ∀^∞ (tie-break 2). Corollaries: log log F(k) ≍ k for expansions of 1, and log log v(k) ≍ k (Erdős Problem 293).

quote_A.text: For every fixed real $C>0$, there are constants $c(C)>0$ and $N_0(C)$ such that, for every integer $N\ge N_0(C)$, \[ \#\{1\le n\le N:p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n\}\ge c(C)N. \]

quote_B.text: It follows that the indices at which $`p_n/n`$ increases have positive lower asymptotic density, answering a question of Erdős and Prachar.

notes: Headline (positive lower density of gaps > C log p for every C) taken as an open question (P2); the Erdős–Prachar question answered affirmatively is a corollary. N_0(C) not explicit → ∀^∞; ∀∃∀^∞ if the density constant c(C) is counted.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected complex curve X, ∀ r ≥1, ∀ quasi-unipotent classes C_1..C_s: ∃ number field L (finite over K) such that M_r(X)(O_L) ∩ Y(C) is Zariski dense in every component of Y

quote_A.text: There is a finite extension $L/K$ such that \[ M_r(X)(\cO_L)\cap Y(\C) \] is Zariski dense in $Y$, and hence in every irreducible component of $Y$.

quote_B.text: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question.

notes: Potential density read as existence of a field L over which density holds (M2; M1 alternative). Litt's question is posed for smooth projective varieties (with a boundary variant); here curves and SL_r only → O5. Lean comparator is an intermediate seam-equation lemma, not the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ D < ∞: ¬∃ infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes with successive distances ≤ D (more strongly ∀D ∃B_D: every component of G_D has ≤ B_D vertices)

quote_A.text: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have bounded steps. More strongly, for each fixed finite step bound, the connected components of the Gaussian-prime graph have uniformly bounded size.

quote_B.text: We prove the Gaussian moat conjecture

notes: Summary leads with the non-existence of infinite bounded-step walks (M4, ∀); the stronger uniform component bound gives ∀∃ with M8. Bound B_D is nonexplicit. If treated as Gordon's open question 'is there an infinite walk?' → P2/O2.

claim_formal: ∀ a ∈ Z with a ≠ −1 and a not a square: ∃^∞ primes p with ord_p(a) = p−1 (quantitatively ≥ c_a x/(log x)² such p in (x,2x) for x ≥ x_a)

quote_A.text: \#\{p\text{ prime}:x<p<2x,\ p\nmid a,\ \ord_p(a)=p-1\} \ge c_a\frac{x}{(\log x)^2}.

quote_B.text: We prove the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture

notes: Headline is the infinitude assertion (∀∃^∞, M2); the quantitative theorem is a lower bound (∀ with M8 alternative). The predicted positive density (quantitative Artin) is not proved; O1 because the paper states the conjecture as the infinitude assertion, O5 if the density form is taken as the posed problem. Side result: uniform zero-free region Re s > 1−10^{-6} for Hecke L-functions of cyclotomic fields ⊇ μ_12. Companion: simultaneous primitive roots conditional on four inputs from the main paper.

claim_formal: ∀ imaginary quadratic K, ∀ elliptic curve E/K: ∃ isobaric automorphic π_E of GL_2(A_K) with r_ι(π_E) ≃ H^1_et(E_K̄, Q̄_l) for all l, ι, and matching local parameters at every place

quote_A.text: There is an isobaric automorphic representation $\pi_E$ of $\GL_2(\A_K)$ with trivial central character and weight zero such that, for every prime $l$

quote_B.text: We prove the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every such curve is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.

notes: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields is posed as its own conjecture (Bianchi modularity), so O1; O5 if the general modularity conjecture over all number fields is taken as the posed problem.

claim_formal: ∀ number fields F_1,F_2, ∀ solvably closed Galois E_i/F_i, ∀ continuous open α: Gal(E_1/F_1) → Gal(E_2/F_2): ∃! field embedding j: E_2 ↪ E_1 inducing α

quote_A.text: Every continuous open homomorphism \[ \alpha:\Gal(E_1/F_1)\longrightarrow\Gal(E_2/F_2) \] is induced by a unique field embedding $j:E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$.

quote_B.text: We prove Uchida's conjecture on open homomorphisms of Galois groups.

notes: Uniqueness was already known (Uchida); new part is existence without kernel or cyclotomic-compatibility restriction.
